classification.difficultyReason: Subtract two corner triangles and solve the resulting quadratic area equation exactly.

content.prompt: A diagonal strip is drawn from one corner of a square to the opposite corner. Find the value of $x$ if the area of the diagonal strip is half the total area of the square.

spec.description: Square with a shaded diagonal strip from lower-left to upper-right, bounded by parallel segments. Each side is divided into lengths x and 1 in the source order. Only the strip is shaded; decorative background shading is omitted.
spec.mathematics: Square side x+1; the two unshaded corner triangles each have perpendicular legs x.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied labels remain; the value of x is absent.

inlines.text: Subtract the two corner triangles from the square.

answer.worked:
The two corner triangles have total area $2\times\dfrac{x^2}{2}=x^2$. Together they occupy half the square.

$$\begin{align*}x^2&=\frac{(x+1)^2}{2}\\2x^2&=x^2+2x+1\\x^2-2x-1&=0\\(x-1)^2&=2\\x-1&=\pm\sqrt{2}\\x&=1\pm\sqrt{2}\end{align*}$$

Since $x$ is a positive length, reject $1-\sqrt{2}$. Hence $x=1+\sqrt{2}$.
